bms_4168_08009a9c.name: bms_rtc_clock_bringup
bms_4168_08009a9c.summary: Start the RTC clock: try LSE with a timeout, fall back to LSI, select it, enable RTC
bms_4168_08009a9c.description: Brings up the RTC clock source in the RCC backup domain. It first tests RTCSEL (RCC.BDCR bits 9:8). If that already selects LSE (0x100), it sets PWR.CR1 DBP (bit 8) to unlock backup-domain writes, clears LSEDRV (BDCR bits 4:3), sets LSEON, and polls LSERDY (BDCR bit 1) for up to 800000 iterations. On success it selects LSE, pulses BDRST (BDCR bit 16) if the select did not take, sets DAT_20000690 to 1 and goes to the end. Otherwise (LSE not selected, or LSE timed out) it clears LSEON and BDCR bit 5 (LSECSSON), sets LSION (RCC.CSR bit 0), polls LSIRDY (CSR bit 1) up to 0x88000 iterations, stores the timeout result in DAT_20000692, selects LSI (RTCSEL = 0x200) with the same BDRST retry, and clears DAT_20000690. The end sets RTCEN (BDCR bit 15).

returns.description: none

bms_4168_08009a9c.notes: Likely defect: the wait counter uVar3 is not reset between the LSE and LSI waits. When LSE was selected and timed out, the counter is already 800000, which is above the LSI bound of 0x88000 (557056). The LSI poll loop then never runs, DAT_20000692 is set to 1 without checking LSIRDY, and LSION is left enabled with no wait. Only the path where RTCSEL was not LSE polls LSI properly. Check the disassembly before relying on the LSI-timeout flag. DAT_20000690 (LSE active) and DAT_20000692 (LSI timeout) are read elsewhere; those readers are not in this packet.

When the accumulator exceeds 2000 it resets to 0 and sets the output byte at 0x20000595 to 1, and that output stays 1 on later high samples until the pin goes low. A low pin clears the output to 0 but leaves the accumulator intact, so high time adds up across interruptions. The function returns the output byte.

returns.description: 0 or 1, the latched output byte at 0x20000595

bms_4139_08009b70.notes: Present in the 4130 and 4139 builds only. The pin's function and the step units are not established here. It is grouped with bms_exti11_irq_disarm, which clears the armed byte at 0x20000594, and the 0x20000594..0x20000596 block. The EXTI line that goes with PB11 is set in SYSCFG EXTICR, which is not visible in this packet.

Called only from bms_4168_08006514.

returns.description: none

bms_4168_08009ba4.notes: The reset pulse is what clears the RTC configuration, so the caller must reprogram it afterwards. The reason it is called from bms_4168_08006514 is not in this packet.

bms_4168_0800a694.name: bms_usart3_rxne_irq_set

In privileged mode the register write is bracketed by isIRQinterruptsEnabled() to save the state, enableIRQinterrupts(1) before the write, and enableIRQinterrupts with the saved bit 0 after it, which is a short interrupt-masked critical section. Unprivileged code skips those calls, so the write is unprotected, and the saved state is reported as 0.
